suggestions.title: Step on the scale in the morning — one read turns four guesses back into numbers

rationale.science: Day-to-day scale moves are mostly water, which is why a missed day costs little — but a trend only exists if reads keep arriving. Eight days without one and the trend is a guess being carried, not a measurement (the same water-vs-fat logic behind DASH-Sodium/Juraschek 2020 cuts both ways).
rationale.data: No weigh-in since 8/21 (162.4). Your app's own gap note now prices your rate anywhere from -0.1 to +0.74 lb/wk — an interval that includes 'not losing at all'.
rationale.relationship: Reads are the one input the trend, the rate, the whoosh verdict and the maintenance estimate all share. One morning read narrows all four at once; nothing else in the app does that.

suggestions.predict: A read lands within a day of this card and the rate interval collapses to a usable number; mid-162s confirms the 8/19-8/21 drop as fat and makes the record official. Blank branch, filed now: no read by 9/01 and the whoosh verdict files VOID - unanswered, not wrong.

suggestions.title: Last call: rough numbers for Fri 8/21 and Sat 8/22 — the weekend bet files void tomorrow

rationale.science: Estimates beat blanks: logging consistency, not logging precision, is what tracks with outcomes (Alhassan 2008). Your own file already treats declared estimate days as first-class — 8/09 is on the books as 'backfilled, rough numbers count'.
rationale.data: Food log ends 8/20. The bet needs exactly two days — Fri 8/21 and Sat 8/22, each over 2,600 to stand — and its hard expiry is 8/30, tomorrow.
rationale.relationship: Those two entries grade the bet on its letter, and they're also the first meals the app's slow-week arithmetic would get to chew on instead of guessing. Two rough entries, two instruments fed.

suggestions.predict: If both land by tomorrow the bet grades on its letter: both over 2,600 and my call stands; both under 2,500 and it's my over-fit, said plainly. Blank branch, pre-filed at the original filing: still blank at tomorrow's run and it files VOID - a design lesson against the forecaster, not a data point about you.

suggestions.title: Put the week on paper — sessions if they happened, one 'rest week' line if they didn't

rationale.science: Layoffs under about two weeks cost a trained lifter essentially nothing — strength and size rebound as if it never happened (Bosquet 2013; Ogasawara 2013). Past that line the losses start to be real. The window is what makes the ask cheap now and expensive later.
rationale.data: Last logged session 8/21 — Monday makes 10 days. No sessions since, and no rest note either, so the file cannot tell a planned deload from a slide.
rationale.relationship: One line converts an unreadable gap into a planned deload, keeps the comeback sheet honest (fresh baselines, openers at 1-2 in reserve), and stops the analysis from inventing stories in the dark.

suggestions.predict: A session or a rest line lands on the next day you touch the app, and next week's brief reads 'deload, resumed on script'. Blank branch: still dark by 9/05 and this stops being a logging ask - the next brief treats it as a real layoff and plans the comeback.
